**Sir Christopher Edward Nolan** (born 30 July 1970) is a British and American filmmaker. Known for his [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles") blockbusters with complex storytelling, Nolan is considered a leading filmmaker of the 21st century. [His films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan_filmography "Christopher Nolan filmography") have earned over $8 billion worldwide, making him [the third-highest-grossing film director of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_film_directors "List of highest-grossing film directors"). [Nolan's accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Christopher_Nolan "List of awards and nominations received by Christopher Nolan") include two [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"), a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award"), and two [British Academy Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards"). He was also appointed a [Commander of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander_of_the_British_Empire "Commander of the British Empire") (CBE) in 2019 and was [knighted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_Bachelor "Knight Bachelor") in 2024 for his contributions to film.
Nolan developed an interest in filmmaking from a young age. After studying [English literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_literature "English literature") at [University College London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_College_London "University College London"), he made several short films before his feature film debut with _[Following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Following "Following")_ (1998). Nolan gained international recognition with his second film, _[Memento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memento_\(film\) "Memento \(film\)")_ (2000), and transitioned into studio filmmaking with _[Insomnia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insomnia_\(2002_film\) "Insomnia \(2002 film\)")_ (2002). He became a high-profile director with [_The Dark Knight_ trilogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman_in_film#The_Dark_Knight_trilogy "Batman in film") (2005–2012) and found further success with _[The Prestige](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Prestige "The Prestige")_ (2006), _[Inception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inception "Inception")_ (2010), _[Interstellar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstellar_\(film\) "Interstellar \(film\)")_ (2014) and _[Dunkirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunkirk_\(2017_film\) "Dunkirk \(2017 film\)")_ (2017). After the release of the critically polarising _[Tenet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenet "Tenet")_ (2020), Nolan parted ways with longtime distributor [Warner Bros. Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Pictures "Warner Bros. Pictures") over their streaming release strategy and signed with [Universal Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures") for the highly successful _[Oppenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oppenheimer_\(film\) "Oppenheimer \(film\)")_ (2023) and _[The Odyssey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Odyssey_\(2026_film\) "The Odyssey \(2026 film\)")_ (2026). The former won him Academy Awards for [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") and [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"). 
Three of Nolan's films have been inducted into the United States [National Film Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Registry "National Film Registry").[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-2) Additionally, two of his films are among the [highest-grossing of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films#Highest-grossing_films "List of highest-grossing films").[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-3) Infused with a [metaphysical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaphysical "Metaphysical") outlook, [his works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematic_style_of_Christopher_Nolan "Cinematic style of Christopher Nolan") thematise [epistemology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistemology "Epistemology"), [existentialism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Existentialism "Existentialism"), ethics, the construction of time and the malleable nature of memory and personal identity. They feature [mathematically inspired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics_and_art "Mathematics and art") images and concepts, unconventional [narrative structures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonlinear_narrative "Nonlinear narrative"), [practical special effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Practical_special_effects "Practical special effects"), experimental soundscapes, [large-format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/70_mm_film "70 mm film") film photography and [materialistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Materialism "Materialism") perspectives. His enthusiasm for the use and preservation of analogue and [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX") film cameras in cinema production, as opposed to digital, has also garnered significant attention. He has co-written several of his films with his brother, [Jonathan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Nolan "Jonathan Nolan"), and runs the production company [Syncopy Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syncopy_Inc. "Syncopy Inc.") with his wife, [Emma Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Thomas "Emma Thomas"). Nolan has been president of the [Directors Guild of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America "Directors Guild of America") since 2025.
## Early life and education
> Just to be clear, I didn't go to film school because I couldn't get into film school. My father knew I wanted to be a filmmaker, but he advised me to get what he referred to as 'a real degree in a real subject,' so I'd have something to fall back on and then you can go to film school afterwards, which turned out not to be the case. So I studied English because that was the academic subject that I was best at and inclined most towards. But what I found when I studied at English at UCL, is it greatly informed my filmmaking process, my writing process. I started to become more at ease with a lot of the literary concepts that underlie film criticism in particular.
— Nolan on his education[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-usatodaycannes-4)
Christopher Edward Nolan was born on 30 July 1970 in the [Westminster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westminster "Westminster") district of London.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-biography_20240310-6) His father, Brendan James Nolan (1936[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-7)–2009),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Shone2014-8) was a British advertising executive of Irish descent[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-9) who worked as a creative director. His mother, Christina Jensen (born 1942),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-10) is an American former flight attendant from [Evanston, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evanston,_Illinois "Evanston, Illinois"); she also worked as a teacher of English. He has an older brother, Matthew, and a younger brother, [Jonathan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Nolan "Jonathan Nolan"), also a filmmaker. The three brothers were raised [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic "Catholic") in [Highgate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highgate "Highgate") and spent their summers in Evanston.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-ft_20230721-11)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-YouTube_PqGrR2Upz0M-12) Nolan also spent time living in Chicago during his youth, and he holds dual British and American citizenship.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-chicagotribune_20140722-13)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202212%E2%80%9313-14)
[![An image showing the top of the oculus in the Flaxman Gallery, University College London](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/Flaxman_Gallery%2C_UCL.JPG/250px-Flaxman_Gallery%2C_UCL.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flaxman_Gallery,_UCL.JPG)Nolan attended [University College London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_College_London "University College London") and used its Flaxman Gallery (pictured) for a scene in _[Inception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inception "Inception")_ (2010).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-filmlondon_20100714-15)
Growing up, Nolan was particularly influenced by the work of [Ridley Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ridley_Scott "Ridley Scott") and the science fiction films _[2001: A Space Odyssey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001:_A_Space_Odyssey "2001: A Space Odyssey")_ (1968) and _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_\(film\) "Star Wars \(film\)")_ (1977).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMooney20184-16)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan2022116,_159-17) He would repeatedly watch the latter film and extensively research its making.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan2022159-18) Nolan began making films at age seven, borrowing his father's [Super 8 camera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_8_film "Super 8 film") and shooting short films with his action figures.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202211,_16-19) These films included a [stop motion animation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop_motion_animation "Stop motion animation") homage to _Star Wars_ called _Space Wars_. He cast his brother Jonathan and built sets from "clay, flour, egg boxes and toilet rolls".[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMooney20184-16) His uncle, who had worked at [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") building guidance systems for the [Apollo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_program "Apollo program") rockets, sent him some launch footage: "I re-filmed them off the screen and cut them in, thinking no-one would notice", Nolan later remarked.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-smh_20141104-20) From age eleven, he aspired to be a professional filmmaker.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-telegraph-21) Between 1981 and 1983, Nolan enrolled at Barrow Hills, a Catholic prep school in [Witley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Witley "Witley"), Surrey.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShone202026-22) In his teenage years, Nolan began making films with Adrien and [Roko Belic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roko_Belic "Roko Belic"). Nolan and Roko co-directed the [surreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrealism "Surrealism") 8 mm _Tarantella_ (1989), which was shown on _Image Union_ , an independent film and video showcase on the [Public Broadcasting Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Broadcasting_Service "Public Broadcasting Service").[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-24)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMooney20185-25)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShone202048-26) In 2021, after a fan posted a copy of _Tarantella_ online, Nolan's production company filed a copyright infringement claim to have the film removed.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-nytimes_20240307-27)
Nolan was [privately educated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_schools_in_the_United_Kingdom "Private schools in the United Kingdom") at [Haileybury and Imperial Service College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haileybury_and_Imperial_Service_College "Haileybury and Imperial Service College") in [Hertford Heath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertford_Heath "Hertford Heath"), Hertfordshire, and later studied [English literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_literature "English literature") at [University College London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_College_London "University College London") (UCL). Having not been accepted to a film school, he pursued "a degree in something unrelated", which his father suggested "gives a different take on things".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMooney20186-28) He chose UCL specifically for its filmmaking facilities, which comprised a [Steenbeck editing suite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steenbeck "Steenbeck") and [16 mm film cameras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16_mm_film#Cameras "16 mm film").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Tempest-29) Nolan was president of UCL's Film Society,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Tempest-29) and with [Emma Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Thomas "Emma Thomas") (his girlfriend and future wife) he screened feature films in [35mm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/35_mm_movie_film "35 mm movie film") during the school year and used the money earned to produce 16 mm films over the summers.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-British_Cinematographer_pt2-30)
He graduated in 1993 with a bachelor's degree in English literature. Thomas, who studied history at UCL and was also active in the Film Society, met Nolan on his first day at his hall of residence, [Ramsay Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halls_of_residence_at_University_College_London "Halls of residence at University College London"). They later married and co-founded the production company [Syncopy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syncopy_Inc. "Syncopy Inc."). Both have retained strong ties with UCL, receiving honorary fellowships (Nolan in 2006, Thomas in 2013). In 2017, Nolan was awarded an honorary doctorate.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-ucl_20240312-31)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-standard_3633651-32)
## Career
### 1993–2003: Early career and breakthrough
After earning his bachelor's degree in English literature in 1993, Nolan worked as a [script reader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Script_analyst "Script analyst"), [camera operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camera_operator "Camera operator") and director of [corporate films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corporate_film "Corporate film") and [industrial films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_films "Industrial films").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Tempest-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Feinberg-33)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-34) He directed, wrote and edited the short film _[Larceny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larceny_\(short_film\) "Larceny \(short film\)")_ (1996),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202234-35) which was filmed over a weekend in black and white with limited equipment and a small cast and crew.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMooney20185-25)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-36) Funded by Nolan and shot with the [UCL Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCL_Union "UCL Union") Film society's equipment, it appeared at the [Cambridge Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge_Film_Festival "Cambridge Film Festival") in 1996 and is considered one of UCL's best shorts.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-37) For unknown reasons, the film has since been removed from public view.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202234-35) Nolan filmed a second short, _[Doodlebug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doodlebug_\(film\) "Doodlebug \(film\)")_ (1997), about a man seemingly chasing an insect with his shoe, only to discover that it is a miniature of himself.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMooney20186-28)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-independent-38)
Nolan and Thomas first attempted to make a feature in the mid-1990s titled _Larry Mahoney_ , which they scrapped.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-independent_39466428-39) During this period in his career, Nolan had little to no success getting his projects off the ground, facing several rejections; he added, "[T]here's a very limited pool of finance in the UK. To be honest, it's a very clubby kind of place ... Never had any support whatsoever from the British film industry."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-AndrewPulver05-40)
Shortly after abandoning _Larry Mahoney_ , Nolan conceived the idea for his first feature, _[Following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Following "Following")_ (1998), which he wrote, directed, photographed and edited. The film depicts an unemployed young writer ([Jeremy Theobald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Theobald "Jeremy Theobald")) who trails strangers through London, hoping they will provide material for his first novel, but is drawn into a criminal underworld when he fails to keep his distance. It was inspired by Nolan's experience of living in London and having his apartment burgled; he observed that the common attribute between larceny and pursuing someone through a crowd was that they both cross social boundaries.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202220%E2%80%9321-41) Co-produced by Nolan with Thomas and Theobald,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShone2020441-42) it was made on a budget of around £3,000. Most of the cast and crew were friends of Nolan, and shooting took place on weekends over the course of a year.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202224,_42-43) To conserve [film stock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_stock "Film stock"), each scene was rehearsed extensively to ensure that the first or second take could be used in the final edit.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMooney20186-28)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Tobias-44) _Following_ won several awards during its festival run and was well received by critics who labelled Nolan a majorly talented debutant.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-45)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202230%E2%80%9331-46) [Scott Timberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Timberg "Scott Timberg") of _[New Times LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Times_LA "New Times LA")_ wrote that it "echoed [Hitchcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hitchcock "Hitchcock") classics", but was "leaner and meaner".[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Timberg-47) [Janet Maslin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Maslin "Janet Maslin") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ was impressed with its "spare look" and "agile hand-held camerawork", saying, "As a result, the actors convincingly carry off the before, during and after modes that the film eventually, and artfully, weaves together."[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-nytimes_958260-48)
> "The difference between shooting _[Following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Following "Following")_ with a group of friends wearing our own clothes and my mum making sandwiches to spending $4 million of somebody else's money on _[Memento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memento_\(film\) "Memento \(film\)")_ and having a crew of a hundred people is, to this day, by far the biggest leap I've ever made."
— Nolan on the jump from his first film to his second (2012)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-seattletimes_20120717-49)
_Following_ 's success afforded Nolan the opportunity to make _[Memento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memento_\(film\) "Memento \(film\)")_ (2000), which became his breakthrough film. His brother Jonathan pitched the idea to him, about a man with [anterograde amnesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterograde_amnesia "Anterograde amnesia") who uses notes and tattoos to hunt for his wife's murderer.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Klein-50) Jonathan worked the idea into a short story, "[Memento Mori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memento_Mori_\(short_story\) "Memento Mori \(short story\)")" (2001), and Nolan developed it into a screenplay that told the story in reverse. Aaron Ryder, an executive for [Newmarket Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newmarket_Films "Newmarket Films"), said it was "perhaps the most innovative script I had ever seen".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMottram2002176-51) The film was optioned and given a budget of $4.5 million,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-weekend-52) with [Guy Pearce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Pearce "Guy Pearce") and [Carrie-Anne Moss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrie-Anne_Moss "Carrie-Anne Moss") in the starring roles.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMottram2002177-53) Newmarket also distributed the film after it was rejected by studios who feared that it would not attract a wide audience. Following a positive [word of mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_of_mouth "Word of mouth") and screenings in 500 theatres, it earned $40 million.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202245%E2%80%9348-54) _Memento_ premiered at the [Venice Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Film_Festival "Venice Film Festival") in September 2000 to critical acclaim.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMottram200262%E2%80%9364-55) [Joe Morgenstern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Morgenstern "Joe Morgenstern") of _[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")_ wrote in his review, "I can't remember when a movie has seemed so clever, strangely affecting and slyly funny at the very same time."[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-wsj_984698693712-56) In the book _The Philosophy of Neo-Noir_ , Basil Smith drew a comparison with [John Locke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Locke "John Locke")'s _[An Essay Concerning Human Understanding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An_Essay_Concerning_Human_Understanding "An Essay Concerning Human Understanding")_ , which argues that conscious memories constitute our identities – a theme Nolan explores in the film.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith200735-57) _Memento_ earned Nolan many accolades, including nominations for an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Writing_\(Original_Screenplay\) "Academy Award for Best Writing \(Original Screenplay\)") and a [Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay"), as well as two [Independent Spirit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Spirit_Award "Independent Spirit Award"): [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Spirit_Award_for_Best_Director "Independent Spirit Award for Best Director") and [Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Spirit_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Independent Spirit Award for Best Screenplay").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-nytimesawards-58)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShone202019-59) Six critics listed it as one of the best [films of the 2000s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000s_in_film "2000s in film").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Metadecade-60) In 2001, Nolan and Emma Thomas founded the production company [Syncopy Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syncopy_Inc. "Syncopy Inc.")[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-syncopy-61)[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-63)
Impressed by his work on _Memento_ , filmmaker [Steven Soderbergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Soderbergh "Steven Soderbergh") recommended Nolan to [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") to direct the [psychological thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychological_thriller "Psychological thriller") _[Insomnia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insomnia_\(2002_film\) "Insomnia \(2002 film\)")_ (2002), although the studio initially wanted a more seasoned director.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEdeWaardTait201349-64) A remake of the 1997 [Norwegian thriller of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insomnia_\(1997_film\) "Insomnia \(1997 film\)"), the film is viewed as "the outlier of Nolan's filmography" due to its perceived lack of unconventionality he is known for.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-joblo_20240513-65)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202250-66) Starring [Al Pacino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Pacino "Al Pacino"), [Robin Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Williams "Robin Williams") and [Hilary Swank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilary_Swank "Hilary Swank"),[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShone2020442-67) _Insomnia_ follows two Los Angeles detectives sent to a northern Alaskan town to investigate the murder of a local teenager. It received positive reviews from critics and earned $113 million against a budget of $46 million.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-rottentomatoes_1114154-68)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-69) Film critic [Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") praised the film for introducing new perspectives and ideas on the issues of morality and guilt, adding, "Unlike most remakes, the Nolan _Insomnia_ is not a pale retread, but a re-examination of the material, like a new production of a good play."[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-rogerebert_20020524-70) [Richard Schickel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Schickel "Richard Schickel") of _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time \(magazine\)")_ deemed _Insomnia_ a "worthy successor" to _Memento_ and "a triumph of atmosphere over a none-too-mysterious mystery".[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-time_238623-71)
_Following_ , _Memento_ and _Insomnia_ established Nolan's image as an "[auteur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auteur "Auteur")".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHill-Parks201526-72) After the lattermost, he wrote a screenplay for a [Howard Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Hughes "Howard Hughes") biopic. Nolan reluctantly tabled his script after learning that [Martin Scorsese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Scorsese "Martin Scorsese") was already making one such film: _[The Aviator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aviator_\(2004_film\) "The Aviator \(2004 film\)")_ (2004).[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202264%E2%80%9365-73) He was then briefly attached to direct a film adaptation of [Ruth Rendell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Rendell "Ruth Rendell")'s novel _[The Keys to the Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Keys_to_the_Street "The Keys to the Street")_ for [Fox Searchlight Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Searchlight_Pictures "Fox Searchlight Pictures") but chose to direct _[Batman Begins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman_Begins "Batman Begins")_ instead.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-chapman-74) In April 2003, filmmaker [David O. Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_O._Russell "David O. Russell") put Nolan in a [headlock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grappling_hold "Grappling hold") at a Hollywood party after learning that [Jude Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jude_Law "Jude Law"), whom Russell wanted to cast, had decided to work with Nolan instead. Russell pressured Nolan to display "artistic solidarity" by relinquishing Law from his cast.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-nytimes_20040919-75)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-vulture-76)
### 2003–2013: Widespread recognition
In early 2003, Nolan was set to direct _[Troy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troy_\(film\) "Troy \(film\)")_ (2004), based on [Homer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homer "Homer")'s _[Iliad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iliad "Iliad")_.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-deadline_521215-77)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-slashfilm_1888064-78)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-indiewire_20130621-79) After leaving _Troy_ , Nolan approached Warner Bros. with the idea of making a new [Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman "Batman") film, based on the character's origin story.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-bb-latimes-80) Nolan was fascinated by the notion of grounding it in a more realistic world than a comic-book fantasy.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202273%E2%80%9375-81) Warner Bros. let Nolan make _[Batman Begins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman_Begins "Batman Begins")_ (2005) to reconcile with him after he was forced out of _Troy_ when [Wolfgang Petersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolfgang_Petersen "Wolfgang Petersen"), the film's producer, decided to direct it.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-NolanTroyConfirm-82) On _Batman Begins_ , Nolan relied heavily on traditional [stunts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stunt "Stunt") and [miniature effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miniature_effect "Miniature effect") during filming, with minimal use of [computer-generated imagery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-generated_imagery "Computer-generated imagery") (CGI).[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202269-83) _Batman Begins_ was the biggest project Nolan had undertaken to that point,[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-84) and it was released to critical acclaim and commercial success.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-rottentomatoes_20050615-85)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-:0-86) Starring [Christian Bale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Bale "Christian Bale") as [Bruce Wayne / Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Wayne_\(Dark_Knight_trilogy\) "Bruce Wayne \(Dark Knight trilogy\)")—along with [Michael Caine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Caine "Michael Caine"), [Gary Oldman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Oldman "Gary Oldman"), [Morgan Freeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Freeman "Morgan Freeman") and [Liam Neeson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Neeson "Liam Neeson")— _Batman Begins_ revived the Batman franchise.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-theatlantic_395477-87)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-mtv_20080814-88) _Batman Begins_ was 2005's ninth-highest-grossing film and was praised for its psychological depth and contemporary relevance;[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-:0-86)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-89) it is cited as one of the most influential films of the 2000s.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-go_31802311-90) Film author Ian Nathan wrote that within five years of his career, Nolan "[went] from unknown to indie darling to gaining creative control over one of the biggest properties in Hollywood, and (perhaps unwittingly) fomenting the genre that would redefine the entire industry".[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202258%E2%80%9359-91)
Nolan directed, co-wrote and produced _[The Prestige](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Prestige "The Prestige")_ (2006), an adaptation of [the Christopher Priest novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Prestige_\(novel\) "The Prestige \(novel\)") about two rival 19th-century magicians.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202278-92) The screenplay was the result of an intermittent, five-year collaboration between him and his brother Jonathan, who had begun writing it in 2001. Nolan initially intended to make the film as early as 2003, but had postponed the project after agreeing to make _Batman Begins_.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202279-93)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-variety_1117884751-94) Starring [Hugh Jackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Jackman "Hugh Jackman") and Christian Bale in the lead roles of rival magicians, _The Prestige_ received critical acclaim and received two Academy Award nominations.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-theguardian_20141128_prestige-95)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-theguardian_20070226_awardsandprizes-96) Roger Ebert described it as "quite a movie – atmospheric, obsessive, almost satanic",[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-rogerebert_20070906-97) and [Kenneth Turan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Turan "Kenneth Turan") of the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ called it an "ambitious, unnerving melodrama".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-latimes_20061020-98) _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_ 's [Philip French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_French "Philip French") wrote: "In addition to the intellectual or philosophical excitement it engenders, _The Prestige_ is gripping, suspenseful, mysterious, moving and often darkly funny."[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-theguardian_20061112_drama-99) Despite a negative box-office prognosis, the film earned over $109 million against a budget of $40 million.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202285,_94%E2%80%9395-100)

_[The Dark Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dark_Knight "The Dark Knight")_ (2008), the follow-up to _Batman Begins_ , was Nolan's next venture. Initially reluctant to make a sequel, he agreed after Warner Bros. repeatedly insisted.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan202296%E2%80%9397-101) Nolan wanted to expand on the [noir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_noir "Film noir") quality of the first film by broadening the canvas and taking on "the dynamic of a story of the city, a large crime story ... where you're looking at the police, the justice system, the vigilante, the poor people, the rich people, the criminals".[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-102) Continuing to minimise the use of CGI, Nolan employed high-resolution [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX") cameras, making it the first major motion picture to use this technology.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJoy201513-103)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-variety_1202875906-104) _The Dark Knight_ has been ranked as one of the best films of the 2000s and one of the [best superhero films ever made](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_films_considered_the_best#Superhero "List of films considered the best").[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-109) Many critics declare _The Dark Knight_ to be "the most successful comic book film ever made".[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZornadoReilly2021166-110) [Manohla Dargis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manohla_Dargis "Manohla Dargis") of _The New York Times_ found the film to be of higher artistic merit than many Hollywood blockbusters: "Pitched at the divide between art and industry, poetry and entertainment, it goes darker and deeper than any Hollywood movie of its comic-book kind."[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Dargis-111) Ebert expressed a similar point of view, describing it as a "haunted film that leaps beyond its origins and becomes an engrossing tragedy".[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-suntimes_55996637-112) _The Dark Knight_ set many box-office records during its theatrical run,[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-nytimes_20080728-113) earning over $1 billion worldwide.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-114) At the [81st Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Academy_Awards "81st Academy Awards"), the film was nominated in eight categories, winning two: [Best Sound Editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Sound_Editing "Academy Award for Best Sound Editing") for [Richard King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_King_\(sound_designer\) "Richard King \(sound designer\)") and a posthumous [Best Supporting Actor award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor") for [Heath Ledger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heath_Ledger "Heath Ledger") for his portrayal of the [Joker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joker_\(The_Dark_Knight\) "Joker \(The Dark Knight\)").[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-oscars_20141007-115) The film's failure to garner a Best Picture nomination was criticised by the media. Beginning in 2010, the [Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences") increased their Best Picture nominees from five to ten, a change known as "The Dark Knight Rule".[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-npr_580219918-116) Nolan received many [awards and nominations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_accolades_received_by_The_Dark_Knight "List of accolades received by The Dark Knight") for his work on the film.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-nytimesawards-58) In the late 2000s, Nolan was reported to direct a film adaptation of the 1960s television series _[The Prisoner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Prisoner "The Prisoner")_.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-chapman-74)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-variety_1235938430-117)
The success of _The Dark Knight_ allowed Warner Bros. to sign Nolan to write, direct and co-produce _[Inception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inception "Inception")_ (2010) – a film for which he had the idea around nine years before its release.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGowan2012147-118) Nolan described the film as "a contemporary sci-fi actioner set within the architecture of the mind".[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Tackles-119) Starring a large ensemble cast led by [Leonardo DiCaprio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_DiCaprio "Leonardo DiCaprio"), the film became a critical and commercial success upon its release.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-collider_20101223-120) Film critic [Mark Kermode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Kermode "Mark Kermode") named it the best [![Christopher Nolan is looking directly towards the camera.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Christopher_Nolan%2C_London%2C_2013_%28crop%29.jpg/250px-Christopher_Nolan%2C_London%2C_2013_%28crop%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Christopher_Nolan,_London,_2013_\(crop\).jpg)Nolan at the 2013 premiere of _[Man of Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_of_Steel_\(film\) "Man of Steel \(film\)")_ in London
Around the release of _[The Dark Knight Rises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dark_Knight_Rises "The Dark Knight Rises")_ (2012), Nolan's third and final Batman film, Joseph Bevan of the [British Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Film_Institute "British Film Institute") wrote a profile on him: "In the space of just over a decade, Christopher Nolan has shot from promising British indie director to undisputed master of a new brand of intelligent escapism."[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-bevan-125) After initial hesitation, Nolan agreed to return to direct _The Dark Knight Rises_ and worked with his brother and [David S. Goyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_S._Goyer "David S. Goyer") to develop a story that he felt would end [the trilogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman_in_film#The_Dark_Knight_trilogy "Batman in film") on a high note.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan2022138%E2%80%93139-126) The film was released to positive reviews.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-nme_275513-127) Kenneth Turan found the film "potent, persuasive and hypnotic" and "more than an exceptional superhero movie, it is masterful filmmaking by any standard".[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-latimes_20120719-128) [Christy Lemire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christy_Lemire "Christy Lemire") of _[HuffPost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HuffPost "HuffPost")_ wrote in her review that Nolan concluded his trilogy in a "typically spectacular, ambitious fashion", but disliked the "overloaded" story and excessive grimness.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-huffingtonpost_1677247-129) _The Dark Knight Rises_ was a box office success, becoming the thirteenth film to gross $1 billion.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-hollywoodreporter_367476-130)
_The Dark Knight_ trilogy inspired a trend in future superhero films seeking to replicate its gritty, realistic tone to little success. The second instalment in particular revitalised the genre at a time when recent superhero films had failed to meet expectations.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Child2015-131)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-theatlantic_565448-132) Ben Child of _The Guardian_ wrote that the three films "will remain thrilling totems of the genre for decades to come".[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Child2015-131) During story discussions for _The Dark Knight Rises_ , Goyer told Nolan of his idea about _[Man of Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_of_Steel_\(film\) "Man of Steel \(film\)")_ (2013), which the latter would produce.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-digitalspy_468532-133) Impressed with [Zack Snyder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zack_Snyder "Zack Snyder")'s work in _[300](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/300_\(film\) "300 \(film\)")_ (2006) and _[Watchmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watchmen_\(2009_film\) "Watchmen \(2009 film\)")_ (2009), Nolan hired him to direct the film.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-nytimes_20130522-134) Starring [Henry Cavill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Cavill "Henry Cavill") as [Clark Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman_\(DC_Extended_Universe\) "Superman \(DC Extended Universe\)") who learns that he is a powerful alien, _Man of Steel_ received mixed reviews and grossed more than $660 million against a budget of $220 million.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-135)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-boxofficemojo_0770828-136)
### 2014–2022: Established filmmaker
[![Jonathan Nolan looking to his left](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Jonathan_Nolan_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg/250px-Jonathan_Nolan_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jonathan_Nolan_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)Nolan and his younger brother, [Jonathan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Nolan "Jonathan Nolan") (_pictured_ in 2017), wrote several screenplays together, including that of _The Dark Knight_ and _Interstellar_.
Nolan next directed, wrote and produced the science-fiction film _[Interstellar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstellar_\(film\) "Interstellar \(film\)")_ (2014). The first drafts of the script were written by Jonathan Nolan, and it was originally to be directed by [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan2022160%E2%80%93161-137) Based on the scientific theories of [theoretical physicist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_physicist "Theoretical physicist") [Kip Thorne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kip_Thorne "Kip Thorne"), the film follows a group of [astronauts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut") who travel through a [wormhole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wormhole "Wormhole") in search of a new home for humanity.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-indiewire_20130110-138) In a 2014 discussion of the film's physics, Nolan expressed his admiration for [scientific objectivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_objectivity "Scientific objectivity"), wishing it were applied "in every aspect of our civilisation".[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-ThorneNolan-139) _Interstellar_ – starring [Matthew McConaughey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_McConaughey "Matthew McConaughey"), [Anne Hathaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Hathaway "Anne Hathaway") and [Jessica Chastain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Chastain "Jessica Chastain") – was released to positive reviews and grossed $773 million worldwide.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-140)[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-boxofficemojo_0816692-141) Observing its "visual dazzle, thematic ambition", _The New York Times_ 's [A. O. Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._O._Scott "A. O. Scott") wrote that _Interstellar_ is a "sweeping, futuristic adventure driven by grief, dread and regret".[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-nytimes_20141104-142) Documentary filmmaker [Toni Myers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Myers "Toni Myers") called the film "a real work of art" and praised it for exploring a story spanning multiple generations.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-cnet_20160610-143) _Interstellar_ was particularly praised for its scientific accuracy, which led to the publication of two [academic papers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_papers "Scientific papers").[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJames_et_al.2015a-144)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJames_et_al.2015b-145) The _[American Journal of Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Journal_of_Physics "American Journal of Physics")_ called for it to be shown in school science lessons.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-bbc_33173197-146)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJames_et_al.2015b486-147) At the [87th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/87th_Academy_Awards "87th Academy Awards"), the film won Best Visual Effects and received four other nominations.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-time_3668006-148) Also in 2014, Nolan and Emma Thomas served as executive producers on _[Transcendence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcendence_\(2014_film\) "Transcendence \(2014 film\)")_ , the directorial debut of his longtime cinematographer [Wally Pfister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wally_Pfister "Wally Pfister").[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-hollywoodreporter_337015-149)
In the mid-2010s, Nolan took part in several ventures for film preservation and distribution of the work of lesser-known filmmakers. His production company, Syncopy, formed a joint venture with [Zeitgeist Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeitgeist_Films "Zeitgeist Films") to release [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") editions of Zeitgeist's films.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-variety_1201437195-150) As a part of the Blu-ray release of the animation films of the [Brothers Quay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brothers_Quay "Brothers Quay"), Nolan directed the documentary short _[Quay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quay_\(film\) "Quay \(film\)")_ (2015). He initiated a theatrical tour, showcasing the Quays' _[In Absentia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_Absentia_\(film\) "In Absentia \(film\)")_ , _The Comb_ and _[Street of Crocodiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_of_Crocodiles "Street of Crocodiles")_. [IndieWire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IndieWire "IndieWire") wrote that the brothers "will undoubtedly have hundreds, if not thousands more fans because of Nolan, and for that _The Quay Brothers in 35mm_ will always be one of [the] latter's most important contributions to cinema".[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-indiewire_20150820-151)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-ew_20150727-152) An advocate for the survival of the analogue medium, Nolan and visual artist [Tacita Dean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tacita_Dean "Tacita Dean") invited representatives from leading American film archives, laboratories and presenting institutions to participate in an informal summit entitled _Reframing the Future of Film_ at the [Getty Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getty_Museum "Getty Museum") in March 2015.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-filmvsdigital_2-153)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-theguardian_20140731_quentin-154) Rufino Tamayo, Mexico City") in Mexico City and [Tata Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tata_Theatre "Tata Theatre") in [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_Picture_&_Television_Fund "Motion Picture & Television Fund") Board of Governors.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-158)
After serving as an executive producer on Zack Snyder's _[Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman_v_Superman:_Dawn_of_Justice "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice")_ (2016) and _[Justice League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice_League_\(film\) "Justice League \(film\)")_ (2017),[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan2022246-159)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan2022247-160) Nolan returned to directing with _[Dunkirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunkirk_\(2017_film\) "Dunkirk \(2017 film\)")_ (2017). Based on his own original screenplay and co-produced with Thomas, the film is set amid World War II in 1940 and the [evacuation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunkirk_evacuation "Dunkirk evacuation") of [Allied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II "Allies of World War II") soldiers from the beaches of [Dunkirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunkirk "Dunkirk"), France. Describing the film as a survival tale with a [triptych](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triptych "Triptych") structure, Nolan wanted to make a "sensory, almost experimental movie" with minimal dialogue.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-161) He said he waited to make _Dunkirk_ until he had earned the trust of a major studio to let him make it as a British film but with an American budget.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-telegraph_20170708-162) Before filming, Nolan sought advice from Spielberg, who later said in an interview with _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety \(magazine\)")_ , "knowing and respecting that Chris [Nolan] is one of the world's most imaginative filmmakers, my advice to him was to leave his imagination, as I did on _[Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saving_Private_Ryan "Saving Private Ryan")_ , in second position to the research he was doing to authentically acquit this historical drama".[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-LangVariety-163) Starring an ensemble cast,[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-variety_1201728153-164) _Dunkirk_ was released to widespread critical acclaim and strong box office results.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-hollywoodreporter_1021889-165)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-166)[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-vanityfair_20170724-167) It grossed over $526 million worldwide, making it the highest-grossing World War II film of all time.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-screenrant_20170915-168) In his review, [Mick LaSalle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_LaSalle "Mick LaSalle") of the _[San Francisco Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Chronicle "San Francisco Chronicle")_ wrote: "It's one of the best [war films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_film "War film") ever made, distinct in its look, in its approach and in the effect it has on viewers. There are movies—they are rare—that lift you out of your present circumstances and immerse you so fully in another experience that you watch in a state of jaw-dropped awe. _Dunkirk_ is that kind of movie."[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-sfgate_11297495-169) The film received [many accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_accolades_received_by_Dunkirk "List of accolades received by Dunkirk"), including Nolan's first Oscar nomination for [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director").[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Sharf-2020-170)
[![A picture showing five people standing on a red carpet](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Cannes_2018_4.jpg/330px-Cannes_2018_4.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cannes_2018_4.jpg)Nolan (right) with [Keir Dullea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keir_Dullea "Keir Dullea"), Katharina Kubrick, Ron Sanders and [Jan Harlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Harlan "Jan Harlan") at the [2018 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Cannes_Film_Festival "2018 Cannes Film Festival")
In 2018, Nolan supervised a new [70 mm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/70_mm_film "70 mm film") print of [Stanley Kubrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Kubrick "Stanley Kubrick")'s _2001: A Space Odyssey_ (1968), made from the [original camera negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Original_camera_negative "Original camera negative"); he presented it at the [2018 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Cannes_Film_Festival "2018 Cannes Film Festival").[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEElsaesser202043-171) _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")_ observed that festival-goers greeted Nolan "like a rock star with a standing ovation".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-usatodaycannes-4) A year later, Nolan and Thomas received executive producer credits on _[The Doll's Breath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doll's_Breath "The Doll's Breath")_ (2019), an animated short directed by the Quay brothers.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Quay-Doll-172)
Nolan's next film was the science fiction film _[Tenet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenet "Tenet")_ (2020), described by [Tom Shone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Shone "Tom Shone") of _[The Sunday Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sunday_Times "The Sunday Times")_ as "a globe-spinning riff on all things Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_David_Washington "John David Washington")) who travels through time to stop a world-threatening underperform at the box-office.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan2022199-177) _Tenet_ was described as his most polarising film; critics praised the ambition and technical aspects but found its story confusing.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-178)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Sharf-2020-170) [Peter Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Bradshaw "Peter Bradshaw") of _The Guardian_ awarded it five out of five, calling it "a cerebral [cadenza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadenza "Cadenza"), a deadpan flourish of crazy implausibility—but supercharged with steroidal energy and and Television Engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_Motion_Picture_and_Television_Engineers "Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers").[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-hollywoodreporter_20201110-182) He served as an executive producer on _[Zack Snyder's Justice League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zack_Snyder's_Justice_League "Zack Snyder's Justice League")_ (2021), a [director's cut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director's_cut "Director's cut") of 2017's _Justice League_.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-insider_20210310-183)
### 2023–present: _Oppenheimer_ and _The Odyssey_
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/ChrisNolanBFI150224_%2810_of_12%29_%2853532289710%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/330px-ChrisNolanBFI150224_%2810_of_12%29_%2853532289710%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ChrisNolanBFI150224_\(10_of_12\)_\(53532289710\)_\(cropped\).jpg)Nolan at [BFI Southbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BFI_Southbank "BFI Southbank") in 2024
Nolan's 12th film was _[Oppenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oppenheimer_\(film\) "Oppenheimer \(film\)")_ (2023), a biopic based on [J. Robert Oppenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Robert_Oppenheimer "J. Robert Oppenheimer") (played by [Cillian Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cillian_Murphy "Cillian Murphy")) and his role in the development of the [atom bomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom_bomb "Atom bomb").[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan2022216-184) It was Nolan's first [R-rated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_Picture_Association_film_rating_system "Motion Picture Association film rating system") film since _Insomnia_ (2002).[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-collider_20230602-185) The film was financed and distributed by [Universal Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures"), making it Nolan's first feature film since _Memento_ that was not made for Warner Bros. He disagreed with Warner Bros.' decision to simultaneously release their films in theatres and on [HBO Max](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO_Max "HBO Max").[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-nme_3282604-186)
Nolan secured the deal with Universal after he was promised a production budget of around $100 million with an equal marketing budget, total creative control, 20% of [first-dollar gross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-dollar_gross "First-dollar gross"), a 100-day theatrical window and a blackout period from the studio wherein the company would not release another film three weeks before or after _Oppenheimer_ 's release.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-hollywoodreporter_1235014132-187) The film received critical acclaim.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-188) Matthew Jackson of _[The A.V. Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_A.V._Club "The A.V. Club")_ wrote, "_Oppenheimer_ deserves the title of masterpiece. It's Christopher Nolan's best film so far, a step up to a new level for one of our finest filmmakers, and a movie that burns itself into your brain."[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-avclub_1850654105-189) Terming it "boldly imaginative and [Nolan's] most mature work yet", [BBC Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Culture "BBC Culture")'s [Caryn James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caryn_James "Caryn James") added that it combined the "explosive, commercially-enticing action of _The Dark Knight_ trilogy" with the "cerebral underpinnings" of _Memento_ , _Inception_ and _Tenet_.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-bbc_20230719-190) _Oppenheimer_ grossed over $975 million worldwide, making it the [third-highest-grossing film of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_in_film#Highest-grossing_films "2023 in film").[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-191) Among the film's [numerous accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_accolades_received_by_Oppenheimer_\(film\) "List of accolades received by Oppenheimer \(film\)"),[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-nytimes_20240107-192)[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-variety_1235913491-193) Nolan won the Academy Awards for Best Director and Best Picture.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-nytimes_20240310-194) The success of _Oppenheimer_ further highlighted Nolan's status as one of Hollywood's most "bankable" directors.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-observer_20260122-195)
In 2025, Nolan was elected president of the [Directors Guild of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America "Directors Guild of America"), a labour organisation representing more than 19,500 members.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-variety_1236525332-196) His next directorial effort was _[The Odyssey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Odyssey_\(2026_film\) "The Odyssey \(2026 film\)")_ , an adaptation of the ancient Greek [epic poem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_poem "Epic poem") the _[Odyssey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odyssey "Odyssey")_ by [Homer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homer "Homer"). It follows [Odysseus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") (portrayed by [Matt Damon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Damon "Matt Damon")), the [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greeks "Greeks") king of [Ithaca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homer's_Ithaca "Homer's Ithaca"), on his perilous journey to return home following the [Trojan War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trojan_War "Trojan War").[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-thewrap_20250217-197) Made on a budget of $250 million, _The Odyssey_ is among the most expensive films of Nolan's career and the first to be shot entirely in [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX")'s [70 mm film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/70_mm_film#IMAX "70 mm film") cameras.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-hollywoodreporter_1236319117-198)[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-hollywoodreporter_1236217925-199)[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-collider_20250516-200) history".[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-time_20260512-202) Leading up to its release, _The Odyssey_ was subject to online backlash and criticism regarding Nolan's Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Bradshaw "Peter Bradshaw") of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_ gave _The Odyssey_ five out of five, calling it ## Personal life and public image
[![Christopher Nolan, on the right, is looking directly towards the camera as Emma Thomas is looking to her right.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Christopher_Nolan_and_Emma_Thomas.jpg/250px-Christopher_Nolan_and_Emma_Thomas.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Christopher_Nolan_and_Emma_Thomas.jpg)Nolan and his wife [Emma Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Thomas "Emma Thomas") in 2011. Thomas has worked as a producer on all of Nolan's films since 1997.
Nolan has been married to [Emma Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Thomas "Emma Thomas") since 1997. They met at [University College London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_College_London "University College London") when Nolan was 19.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-telegraph-21)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-British_Cinematographer_pt2-30) Thomas has worked as a producer on all of Nolan's films since 1997, the same year they were married.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-syncopy-61)[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-abc11_1237089-210) The couple have four children and reside in Los Angeles.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-empireonline_20200818-211) Nolan and Thomas were included in the _[Sunday Times Rich List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunday_Times_Rich_List "Sunday Times Rich List")_ of [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunday_Times_Rich_List_2026 "Sunday Times Rich List 2026") with an estimated [net worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Net_worth "Net worth") of £370 million.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-thetimes_20250516-212)
Nolan prefers to maintain a certain level of mystery about his work.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJoy20153-213) Refusing to discuss his personal life,[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Lewis-Kraus-214) he feels that too much biographical information about a filmmaker detracts from the experience of his audiences. He stated, "I actually don't want people to have me in mind at all when they're watching the films."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Feinberg-33) He does not own a smartphone or have an email address, preferring to hand-deliver his scripts to actors instead and have his wife handle outreach with producers and distributors.[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-people_7561275-215) Unlike most of his filmmaker peers, Nolan is known for wearing [suit jackets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suit_jacket "Suit jacket") on set, describing them as a "uniform" that simplifies his daily routine and allows him to focus on work.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-216)[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-faroutmagazine_20241203-217)[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Lewis-Kraus-214)
## Filmmaking style
Main article: [Cinematic style of Christopher Nolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematic_style_of_Christopher_Nolan "Cinematic style of Christopher Nolan")
Nolan's films are largely centred in [metaphysical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaphysical "Metaphysical") themes, exploring the concepts of time, [memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory "Memory") and [personal identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_identity "Personal identity").[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoh20224,_76-218)[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlouin2013145%E2%80%93146,_149-219) His work is characterised by [mathematically inspired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics_and_art "Mathematics and art") ideas and images, unconventional [narrative structures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonlinear_narrative "Nonlinear narrative"), [materialistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Materialism "Materialism") perspectives, and evocative use of music and sound.[[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-223) Filmmaker [Guillermo del Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillermo_del_Toro "Guillermo del Toro") called Nolan "an emotional mathematician".[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-cbr_20220530-224) [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")'s arts editor [Will Gompertz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Gompertz "Will Gompertz") described him as "an art house auteur making intellectually ambitious blockbuster movies that can leave your pulse racing and your head spinning".[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Gompertz-20-225) Joseph Bevan wrote, "His films allow arthouse regulars to enjoy superhero flicks and multiplex crowds to engage with labyrinthine plot conceits."[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-bevan-125) Nolan views himself as "an indie filmmaker working inside the studio system".[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMolloy201340-226)
> "Christopher Nolan doesn't make sense. And that is exactly how he likes it. In twenty-three years and through twelve films, he has defied the laws of Hollywood by creating startling, original genre pieces that have revelled in their own complexity, confounding every maxim by which the studios hope to appeal to the widest audience. And yet he does that too. Cinemas fill on the possibility of the next Nolan film. Whatever form it might take."
— Film author Ian Nathan on Nolan as a filmmaker (2022)[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan20225-227)
In the sixteen-essay book _The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan_ , professional philosophers and writers analysed Nolan's work; they identified themes of self-destruction, the nature and value of the truth, and the political mindset of the hero and villain, among others.[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTELB2017Description-228) Robbie B. H. Goh, a professor of English literature, described Nolan as a "philosophical filmmaker" who includes philosophical ideas—[existentialism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Existentialism "Existentialism"), [morality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morality "Morality"), [epistemology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistemology "Epistemology") and the distinction between appearance and reality—in films that frequently portray suspense, action and violence. Goh appreciated his ability to incorporate such themes in films that possess "elements of the Hollywood blockbuster"—which help keep the audiences engaged—but simultaneously remain "more thoughtful and self-reflexive than the typical consumerist action film".[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoh20221%E2%80%934-229) He further wrote that Nolan's body of work reflect "a heterogeneity of conditions of products" extending from low-budget films to lucrative blockbusters, "a wide range of genres and settings" and "a diversity of styles that trumpet his versatility".[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoh202212%E2%80%9313-230)
[David Bordwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bordwell "David Bordwell"), a [film theorist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_theorist "Film theorist"), wrote that Nolan has been able to blend his "experimental impulses" with the demands of mainstream entertainment, describing his oeuvre as "experiments with cinematic time by means of techniques of subjective viewpoint and crosscutting".[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-Bordwell2019-231) Nolan's use of practical, in-camera effects, miniatures and models, as well as shooting on celluloid film, has been highly influential in early [21st century cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_cinema_in_21st_century "Hollywood cinema in 21st century").[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJoy20157-232)[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-IndieW-19-233) IndieWire wrote in 2019 that Nolan "kept a viable alternate model of big-budget filmmaking alive", in an era where blockbuster filmmaking has become "a largely computer-generated art form".[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-IndieW-19-233) Because of Nolan's deep involvement in the technical facet of his films, Stuart Joy described him as a "complete filmmaker", who "oversees all aspects of production while also managing cultural and industrial factors outside of the text".[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJoy20156-234)

## Awards and honours
Main article: [List of awards and nominations received by Christopher Nolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Christopher_Nolan "List of awards and nominations received by Christopher Nolan")
[![A hand and footprint reading "Christopher Nolan" at the top and "7/7/2012" at the bottom.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Christopher_Nolan_TCL.jpg/250px-Christopher_Nolan_TCL.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Christopher_Nolan_TCL.jpg)Nolan's hand and shoeprints in front of the [Grauman's Chinese Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauman's_Chinese_Theatre "Grauman's Chinese Theatre") in Los Angeles
Nolan has been nominated for eight [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") (winning two), eight [British Academy Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards") (winning two) and six [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award") (winning one).[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-nytimesawards-58)[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-FOOTNOTENathan2022197-277)[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-allmovie_240025-278)[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-279) From 2011 to 2014, he appeared in [_Forbes_ Celebrity 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes_Celebrity_100 "Forbes Celebrity 100") list based on his income and popularity.[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-280) Nolan appeared in _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time \(magazine\)")_ 's [100 most influential people in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100") in 2015.[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-time_3822892-281)
Nolan was named an Honorary Fellow of UCL in 2006,[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-282) and conferred an honorary doctorate in literature in 2017.[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-ucl_20170912-283) In 2012, he became the youngest director to receive a hand-and-footprint ceremony at [Grauman's Chinese Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauman's_Chinese_Theatre "Grauman's Chinese Theatre") in Los Angeles.[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-ew_20120707-284) He was appointed Commander of the [Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_British_Empire "Order of the British Empire") in the [2019 New Year Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_New_Year_Honours "2019 New Year Honours") for services to film.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-whoswho-1)[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-285) In 2023, he was awarded the [Federation of American Scientists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_of_American_Scientists "Federation of American Scientists")' Public Service Award for his depiction of scientists in his film _Oppenheimer_.[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-deadline_1235569081-286)
In 2024, Nolan received the [British Film Institute Fellowship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Film_Institute_Fellowship "British Film Institute Fellowship") in recognition of his "extraordinary achievements and enormous contribution to cinema,"[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-hollywoodreporter_1235709538-287) and the [Honorary César](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_C%C3%A9sar "Honorary César") award from the [Académie des Arts et Techniques du Cinéma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acad%C3%A9mie_des_Arts_et_Techniques_du_Cin%C3%A9ma "Académie des Arts et Techniques du Cinéma") for "continually push[ing] the boundaries of storytelling."[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-deadline_1235797659-288) In March 2024, Nolan was made a [knight bachelor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_bachelor "Knight bachelor") for his contributions to film,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-whoswho-1) while his wife Emma Thomas was honoured with a damehood.[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-289)[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan#cite_note-bbc_68683313-290)
